heading_path: The discount in the cart is different from the product page › 1. The product page counts quantity already in the cart
section: 1. The product page counts quantity already in the cart
summary: Why the tier discount shown on the product page differs from the cart, usually the count mode, quantity already in the cart, margin protection, or a market in its own currency.
text:
The live price on the product page adds the quantity you are about to add to
whatever is already in the cart that counts toward the same tier (same
variant, same product, or same tier set, depending on the count mode). If the
product page and the cart still disagree, first reproduce both with the same
starting cart in [try-a-cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md).

doc_title: The discount in the cart is different from the product page
heading_path: The discount in the cart is different from the product page › 2. The count mode
summary: Why the tier discount shown on the product page differs from the cart, usually the count mode, quantity already in the cart, margin protection, or a market in its own currency.
text:
Per line, per product or per cart (Pro) all count differently. "Per line"
counts each cart line on its own — the same variant added with different
line properties or a different selling plan is a separate line and does not
add up with it. A quantity split across several lines of the same product
only adds up under "per product" or "per cart". See
[../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).

doc_title: The discount in the cart is different from the product page
heading_path: The discount in the cart is different from the product page › 3. Margin protection lowered it, or the market has its own currency
section: 3. Margin protection lowered it, or the market has its own currency
summary: Why the tier discount shown on the product page differs from the cart, usually the count mode, quantity already in the cart, margin protection, or a market in its own currency.
text:
The product page's cap never promises more than checkout's, but it can lag
behind it: in a market with its own currency it converts the price floor
using Shopify's exchange rate, and a variant whose floor is still being
computed shows no discount promise at all rather than a guess. See
[tier-lowered-by-margin-protection](tier-lowered-by-margin-protection.md).

doc_title: The discount in the cart is different from the product page
heading_path: The discount in the cart is different from the product page › 4. A product discount beat the tier
section: 4. A product discount beat the tier
summary: Why the tier discount shown on the product page differs from the cart, usually the count mode, quantity already in the cart, margin protection, or a market in its own currency.
text:
A tier competes with other product discounts on the same item; the product
page shows the tier, but a code or automatic discount the shopper adds later
can win instead if it is better. See
[../concepts/combining-discounts.md](../concepts/combining-discounts.md).

doc_title: The discount in the cart is different from the product page
heading_path: The discount in the cart is different from the product page › 5. The tier set is not synced yet
section: 5. The tier set is not synced yet
summary: Why the tier discount shown on the product page differs from the cart, usually the count mode, quantity already in the cart, margin protection, or a market in its own currency.
text:
A tier set just changed can take a short moment to reach the storefront block
and the checkout function separately; they read the same source but not at the
exact same instant. See [../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).

For a checkout difference that is not about quantity tiers, see
[checkout-discount-differs](checkout-discount-differs.md).

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
**First reproduce it** in [Try a cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md) with the same products,
market, codes and day. Try a cart runs the same engine as checkout and explains each
discount. Then check, in this order:

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 1. The change is not in Shopify yet
section: 1. The change is not in Shopify yet
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
Saved is not the same as live. While a discount is "Not synced" (or the last sync
failed), checkout runs the previous state. Open the Overview and **Sync again**. See
[../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 2. A collection changed a moment ago
section: 2. A collection changed a moment ago
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
A product just added to or removed from a collection reaches checkout within
minutes. **Refresh targeting** on the Overview does it now.

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 3. A discount outside Won applies too
section: 3. A discount outside Won applies too
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
A Shopify discount or another app's discount can add to Won's, or block it if it does
not combine. Won does not see it. Check **Discounts outside Won** on the Overview.
See [../concepts/discounts-outside-won.md](../concepts/discounts-outside-won.md).

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 4. The combining rules
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
Two product discounts on the same item do not add up; the better one wins. The order
discount is taken from the subtotal after product discounts. See
[../concepts/combining-discounts.md](../concepts/combining-discounts.md).

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 5. Margin protection lowered it
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text: See [discount-lowered-by-margin-protection](discount-lowered-by-margin-protection).

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 6. Currency, market or dates
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
- No value in the cart's currency: the discount is not offered there
  ([discount-not-offered-in-a-currency](discount-not-offered-in-a-currency)).
- Dates are whole days in the shop's time zone, and the end day is included.

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 7. Small, known differences
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
- A percentage that lands exactly on half a cent: Shopify may round 1 cent the other
  way.
- A fixed shipping discount when an order ships in several parts applies to the first
  shipment only.
- A cart with very many discounts can hit Shopify's output size limit; checkout then
  gives slightly less. Try a cart shows the exact amount.

doc_title: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected
heading_path: The discount at checkout differs from what I expected › 8. A Pro setting on a Free shop
section: 8. A Pro setting on a Free shop
summary: Why checkout gives a different discount than expected, in the order to check, and how to reproduce it in Try a cart.
text:
Pro settings stay saved but checkout does not run them on Free. The Overview lists
them. See [../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md](../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md).

doc_title: A price did not come back after a clearance sale
heading_path: A price did not come back after a clearance sale
summary: Won restores only prices that still hold the sale value; a price you changed during the sale is kept, and the sale's history says so.
text:
Won restores a price only if it still holds the value the sale set. If you (or
another app) changed the price, the compare-at price or a price list's fixed
price while the sale ran, Won keeps your change. The sale's **history** then
shows "A price changed outside the app was kept".

**Fix:** set the price you want in Shopify yourself; Won does not touch it again.

If the history says "Restoring the prices failed; it is retried", Shopify did not
answer; Won retries after 1, 5, 15 and then every 60 minutes, and the sale keeps
its sale mark until the prices are back.

doc_title: The clearance quota is not counting sold pieces
heading_path: The clearance quota is not counting sold pieces
summary: Until Shopify approves the app's access to orders, the clearance quota is not counted; the sale ends by its end date or by hand.
text:
The quota counts the pieces sold in orders. Shopify gives an app the orders only
after it approves the app's access to **protected customer data**. Until then
the Clearance screen and its Overview card say:

> The quota is not counted yet — the sale ends by its date or by hand.

What it means for a running sale:

- "Sold" stays at 0 and "left" stays at the full quota; cancellations and
  refunds are not counted either.
- The sale **does not end by selling out**. It ends at its end date (the start
  of that day in your store's time zone) or when you click **End sale**.
- Prices come back at the end as usual.

What to do: give every sale an **end date** when you start it (the form reminds
you), or end it by hand when the stock is gone. Once the access is approved, the
warning disappears and new orders count; orders placed before that are not
counted back.

See [../concepts/clearance.md](../concepts/clearance.md).

doc_title: More pieces sold than the clearance quota
heading_path: More pieces sold than the clearance quota
summary: An order can reach Won a moment after checkout; pieces sold in that moment count past the quota and the sale shows the exact number.
text:
Shopify tells Won about an order right after checkout, not during it. When the
last pieces of a quota sell in several checkouts at the same moment, a few
pieces can sell at the sale price before Won ends the sale. The sale then shows
"N pc sold past the quota" with the exact number, and its history lists them.

This is expected and cannot be prevented by an app. Keep the quota a little below
the stock you want to clear if that matters.

doc_title: A discount code did not apply to a clearance item
heading_path: A discount code did not apply to a clearance item
summary: A clearance item takes no other discount by default; switch Clearance with other discounts on in Settings to allow it.
text:
By default a clearance item takes **no other Won discount**: not a product
discount, not a code, and it is left out of order discounts. The rest of the
cart gets them as usual.

To let clearance items take other discounts too, switch on **Clearance with
other discounts** in **Settings**. The quantity tiers table then also shows
for a variant on sale. See [../concepts/combining-discounts.md](../concepts/combining-discounts.md).

doc_title: A discount code did not apply
heading_path: A discount code did not apply
summary: The reasons a Won discount code gives nothing or is shown as not applicable, and how to find which one applies to a given cart.
text:
Enter the code in [Try a cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md) with the customer's products,
market and day. It says for each code why it applies or not. The usual reasons:

doc_title: A discount code did not apply
heading_path: A discount code did not apply › The code is not live
summary: The reasons a Won discount code gives nothing or is shown as not applicable, and how to find which one applies to a given cart.
text:
- The code discount is switched off, has no code yet, or is not in Shopify yet
  (status "Not synced"). See
  [../reference/discount-statuses.generated.md](../reference/discount-statuses.generated.md).
- It has not started yet, or has ended. Dates are whole days in the shop's time zone.
- The code belongs to a discount **outside Won**: Won does not count it
  ([discount-outside-won](discount-outside-won)).

doc_title: A discount code did not apply
heading_path: A discount code did not apply › The cart does not qualify
summary: The reasons a Won discount code gives nothing or is shown as not applicable, and how to find which one applies to a given cart.
text:
- **Minimum not met**: an amount or a number of items. Check whether the minimum
  counts the whole cart or only the selected products.
- **Not for these products**: the code targets other products or collections.
- **Not valid in this currency**: the discount has no value for the cart's currency
  ([discount-not-offered-in-a-currency](discount-not-offered-in-a-currency)).
- **Not valid in this market** (Pro market targeting).

doc_title: A discount code did not apply
heading_path: A discount code did not apply › Another discount wins
summary: The reasons a Won discount code gives nothing or is shown as not applicable, and how to find which one applies to a given cart.
text:
- **A better discount** already applies to the same items. Two product discounts do
  not add up, so the code gives nothing and Shopify shows it as not applicable
  ([../concepts/combining-discounts.md](../concepts/combining-discounts.md)).
- **Two codes of the same discount**: only one of them applies.
- **Margin protection**: the items are already at their lowest allowed price, so the
  code saves nothing there
  ([discount-lowered-by-margin-protection](discount-lowered-by-margin-protection)).
- **Pro stack with two codes**: Shopify shows one code as not applicable, but its
  value is included in the other ([../concepts/pro-combinations.md](../concepts/pro-combinations.md)).

doc_title: A discount code did not apply
heading_path: A discount code did not apply › Shopify's own limits
summary: The reasons a Won discount code gives nothing or is shown as not applicable, and how to find which one applies to a given cart.
text:
The code's total usage limit is used up, or a once-per-customer code was already used
by this customer. Shopify counts and enforces these.

doc_title: A discount code and the gift
heading_path: A discount code and the gift
summary: What happens to the gift when a discount code takes the order below the threshold, with and without counting other discounts.
text:
It depends on **Count other discounts toward the gift threshold** in
**Cart rewards**:

doc_title: A discount code and the gift
heading_path: A discount code and the gift › Off (the default)
summary: What happens to the gift when a discount code takes the order below the threshold, with and without counting other discounts.
text:
The threshold is the price of the items before discounts. A code never takes
the gift away; the customer gets both.

doc_title: A discount code and the gift
heading_path: A discount code and the gift › On
summary: What happens to the gift when a discount code takes the order below the threshold, with and without counting other discounts.
text:
The threshold counts after discounts in the cart. When the customer enters a
code in the cart's code field and the order drops below the threshold, the
cart warns first and lets them choose:

- **Keep the code (no gift)** — the gift leaves the cart;
- **Remove the code** — the code is removed and the gift stays.

A code entered **only at checkout** keeps the gift: checkout never takes away
a gift the cart already added. That is why the cart has its own code field.

doc_title: A discount code and the gift
heading_path: A discount code and the gift › The code itself does not apply
section: The code itself does not apply
summary: What happens to the gift when a discount code takes the order below the threshold, with and without counting other discounts.
text:
The cart says "Code X does not apply to this cart." The code may be for other
products, may have ended, or may not combine with the cart's discounts. See
[code-not-applied](code-not-applied).

More: [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

doc_title: The discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The discount is lower because of margin protection › How to tell
summary: How to tell that margin protection lowered a discount, why it did, and what to change if the result is not what you want.
text:
- [Try a cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md) marks the item with the margin floor and says
  "The discount on an item is lowered from … to …".
- The discount editor notes that protection lowers the discount.
- With Pro, **Where protection steps in** lists each discount and variant, and by how
  much.

doc_title: The discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The discount is lower because of margin protection › Why it happened
summary: How to tell that margin protection lowered a discount, why it did, and what to change if the result is not what you want.
text:
Margin protection is on and the full discount would take the item below its lowest
allowed price:

- **With a cost price**: the price after discounts must keep your minimum margin,
  measured like Shopify's product margin, from the price the customer pays (tax
  included for tax-inclusive prices).
- **Without a cost price**: the discount is capped at the ceiling percentage.

A product discount is cut to that floor. An order discount is lowered, or leaves out
the items already at their floor. Checkout still goes through; protection never
blocks.

doc_title: The discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The discount is lower because of margin protection › What you can change
summary: How to tell that margin protection lowered a discount, why it did, and what to change if the result is not what you want.
text:
- Lower the **minimum margin**, or the ceiling for products without a cost price.
- Add missing **cost prices** in Shopify: a product with a real cost price is limited
  by its margin, not by the ceiling
  ([products-without-cost-price](products-without-cost-price)).
- With Pro, give a collection its own values
  ([../concepts/margin-per-collection.md](../concepts/margin-per-collection.md)).
- Or turn protection off. Then Won discounts apply in full.

Protection does not touch shipping discounts or discounts outside Won. Background:
[../concepts/margin-protection.md](../concepts/margin-protection.md).

doc_title: The discount is not offered in EUR (or another currency)
heading_path: The discount is not offered in EUR (or another currency) › The usual cause: no value for that currency
section: The usual cause: no value for that currency
summary: Why a Won discount works in one currency but not in another (a missing value, never converted), and how to fix it.
text:
Won never converts amounts by exchange rate. A **fixed amount** and a **minimum order
amount** each need their own value for every currency. Without it, the discount is
not offered in that currency. The Overview warns: "isn't offered in EUR. The value is
missing."

**Fix:** open the discount in **Discounts & codes** and fill in the amount in EUR,
and the minimum in EUR if the discount has a minimum.

A percentage discount needs no amount, but if it has a minimum order amount only in
CZK, it is not offered in EUR.

doc_title: The discount is not offered in EUR (or another currency)
heading_path: The discount is not offered in EUR (or another currency) › Other causes
summary: Why a Won discount works in one currency but not in another (a missing value, never converted), and how to fix it.
text:
- **The discount was moved from Shopify.** It came with the shop currency only; add
  the others.
- **Market targeting (Pro)**: the discount is limited to markets that do not include
  the customer's country. On Free a market-limited discount does not apply at all.
- **The market is switched off in Won**: a discount that targets only switched-off
  markets shows "Not running".
- **No price in that currency**: Try a cart cannot calculate a product that has no
  price in the chosen market's currency.

Check with [Try a cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md) and the EUR market: it says "has no
amount for EUR, so it is not offered here" when the value is missing. Background:
[../concepts/markets-and-currencies.md](../concepts/markets-and-currencies.md).

heading_path: A discount outside Won › What the warning means
summary: What the "discounts outside Won" warning means, why it matters for checkout and margin protection, and what to do with each such discount.
text:
The Overview found a live discount that does not run through Won: one created in
Shopify's Discounts page or by another app. Won's engine does not count it.

heading_path: A discount outside Won › Why it matters
summary: What the "discounts outside Won" warning means, why it matters for checkout and margin protection, and what to do with each such discount.
text:
- Checkout may give a different total than Won shows, because that discount can add
  to Won's or block it.
- Margin protection does not guard it.
- If it uses the same code as a Won discount, the Won discount cannot go live:
  Shopify allows a code on one discount only.

heading_path: A discount outside Won › What to do
summary: What the "discounts outside Won" warning means, why it matters for checkout and margin protection, and what to do with each such discount.
text:
- **Movable**: click **Move**. The dialog says what is lost (for example the usage
  count). Steps: [../tasks/move-native-discounts.md](../tasks/move-native-discounts.md).
- **Not movable**: the Overview says why (for example Buy X get Y, another app's
  discount, a discount for specific customers). Keep it in Shopify knowing Won does
  not count it, or end it in Shopify if Won's discounts replace it.
- **Clash on a code**: move the Shopify discount into Won, or change the code of the
  Won discount.

heading_path: A discount outside Won › After uninstalling
summary: What the "discounts outside Won" warning means, why it matters for checkout and margin protection, and what to do with each such discount.
text:
Discounts moved into Won stop working when the app is uninstalled. Undo the moves
first ([../tasks/undo-a-move.md](../tasks/undo-a-move.md)).

Background: [../concepts/discounts-outside-won.md](../concepts/discounts-outside-won.md).

doc_title: Free shipping or the gift is missing in a market
heading_path: Free shipping or the gift is missing in a market
summary: A reward is offered only in currencies that have their own amount; the admin names the market without one.
text:
Rewards have an amount **per currency**, never converted by exchange rate. A
market whose currency has no amount gets no free shipping or gift, and its
cart shows no progress for it.

**Cart rewards** shows a note under the reward, for example "No amount in EUR
(Slovakia): the reward is not offered in that market." Enter the amount in that
currency and save.

doc_title: Free shipping or the gift is missing in a market
heading_path: Free shipping or the gift is missing in a market › Still missing after you entered it
section: Still missing after you entered it
summary: A reward is offered only in currencies that have their own amount; the admin names the market without one.
text:
- Check the shipping: free shipping also follows the combination switches in
  Settings; a discount that does not combine with shipping leaves it out. See
  [../tasks/switch-combination-categories.md](../tasks/switch-combination-categories.md).
- A change just saved can take a short moment to reach checkout. See
  [../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).

More: [../concepts/markets-and-currencies.md](../concepts/markets-and-currencies.md),
[../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
Checkout makes **1 item** of a gift free when the order reaches the gift's
threshold. Check in this order:

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout › 1. The order is below the threshold
section: 1. The order is below the threshold
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
The threshold counts the items before discounts, without the gift. When the
customer removed items, the cart on your store removes the gift; a gift line
left in the cart below the threshold is paid. **Try a cart** with the same
items shows how much is missing.

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout › 2. More than one item of the gift
section: 2. More than one item of the gift
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
Only 1 item is free. A quantity of 2 on the gift line, or the same gift added a
second time, is paid for the extra items.

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout › 3. The line is not the gift Won offers
section: 3. The line is not the gift Won offers
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
Only the variants you picked for that threshold (or its fallback) are free,
and only on the line the cart added as the gift. The same product added to the
cart the usual way is an ordinary item. A gift you changed in the admin after
the customer added the old one is paid; the customer can remove it.

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout › 4. No threshold in the cart's currency
section: 4. No threshold in the cart's currency
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
A market whose currency has no gift threshold gets no gift. See
[free-shipping-missing-in-a-market](free-shipping-missing-in-a-market).

doc_title: The gift is charged at checkout
heading_path: The gift is charged at checkout › 5. The change is not synced yet
section: 5. The change is not synced yet
summary: Why a gift line is paid at checkout, in the order to check, from the order being below the threshold to a second item of the gift.
text:
A threshold or gift just saved can take a short moment to reach checkout.
Check the Overview for a sync error. See
[../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).

More: [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text: Check in this order:

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 1. The app embed is off
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
The gift is added by the cart on your store, which needs the app embed.
**Cart rewards** shows its state; **Turn on in theme** fixes it. See
[../tasks/add-the-cart-panel-to-the-cart-page.md](../tasks/add-the-cart-panel-to-the-cart-page.md).

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 2. The customer declined it
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
After **No thanks** (or removing the gift by hand) the gift does not come back
in that cart, even when more is added. A new cart offers it again.

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 3. The customer has to choose
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
With a choice of gifts (Pro), the cart asks the customer which one; nothing is
added until they pick.

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 4. The gift is sold out
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
A sold-out gift is not offered and the cart says so. Restock it, or set a
**Fallback gift when it is sold out** for the threshold.

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 5. The order is below the threshold, or the currency has none
section: 5. The order is below the threshold, or the currency has none
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
The threshold counts the items before discounts, without the gift, in the
cart's currency. See
[free-shipping-missing-in-a-market](free-shipping-missing-in-a-market).

doc_title: The gift is not added to the cart
heading_path: The gift is not added to the cart › 6. The cart has not refreshed yet
section: 6. The cart has not refreshed yet
summary: Why the cart does not add the gift, in the order to check, from the app embed being off to the customer having declined it.
text:
The cart adds the gift after the customer changes the cart (adds an item,
changes a quantity) — never just by opening a page. Some themes refresh the
cart drawer only after a reload.

More: [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

doc_title: A product did not get the global quantity tiers
heading_path: A product did not get the global quantity tiers › Why it happened
summary: A product with no quantity tiers is covered by a scoped Pro set that excludes it; only one tier set ever applies per product, scoped sets before the global one.
text:
Exactly one tier set applies to a product: a set scoped to that product, then
a set scoped to one of its collections, then the one global set — the first
match wins, the rest are not even considered. See
[../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).

If the product is included in a Pro product- or collection-scoped set (even
one with **no breaks**, or switched off in a way that still claims the
product), it never falls through to the global set. This is intentional: a
scoped set is how you give a product different — often lower — tiers than the
default, or none at all.

doc_title: A product did not get the global quantity tiers
heading_path: A product did not get the global quantity tiers › How to check
summary: A product with no quantity tiers is covered by a scoped Pro set that excludes it; only one tier set ever applies per product, scoped sets before the global one.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Quantity discounts** and look at each scoped set's product and
   collection list for this product.
2. If a scoped set claims it, remove the product (or its collection) from that
   set's scope, or add breaks to that set, to change what it gets.
3. If no scoped set claims it, check that the global set itself has breaks and
   is not empty.

doc_title: A product did not get the global quantity tiers
heading_path: A product did not get the global quantity tiers › On Free
summary: A product with no quantity tiers is covered by a scoped Pro set that excludes it; only one tier set ever applies per product, scoped sets before the global one.
text:
Scoped sets are a Pro feature. If the shop was Pro and is now on Free, scoped
sets are not deleted, only switched off, so the product they excluded keeps
getting **no** tiers rather than unexpectedly falling into the global set. See
[../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md](../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md).

heading_path: Products without a cost price › What happens to them
summary: What margin protection does with products that have no cost price in Shopify, where to find them, and how to add the cost so Won picks it up.
text:
Margin protection cannot compute a margin without a cost price, so their discount is
capped at **"Products without a cost price: discount at most"**. The same ceiling
protects products whose cost price has not been read yet.

heading_path: Products without a cost price › Where to find them
summary: What margin protection does with products that have no cost price in Shopify, where to find them, and how to add the cost so Won picks it up.
text:
**Margin protection → Cost prices** shows how many variants have a cost price, how
many products have none, and a list of them with a link to add it in Shopify.

heading_path: Products without a cost price › How to fix it
summary: What margin protection does with products that have no cost price in Shopify, where to find them, and how to add the cost so Won picks it up.
text:
Add the cost per item in Shopify on the product, in the variant's pricing. Won picks
it up within minutes by itself; once a day all cost prices are checked as well.
**Refresh cost prices** reads them now.

heading_path: Products without a cost price › Common questions
summary: What margin protection does with products that have no cost price in Shopify, where to find them, and how to add the cost so Won picks it up.
text:
**"Cost prices: not read yet".** They are read only while protection is on. Turn it
on and save; the reading runs in the background and shows its progress.

**The ceiling is higher than my real margin allows.** The ceiling does not know the
cost. A product whose cost is 70 % of its price keeps the full ceiling, which can be
below cost. Add its cost price.

**A product has a cost price, but Won treats it as missing.** In a cart in another
currency the cost price must be converted with Shopify's rate; if that is not
possible, the ceiling applies. If Shopify refused to store a cost price for checkout,
the stricter of the previous cost and the ceiling applies; the page says so.

Background: [../concepts/cost-prices.md](../concepts/cost-prices.md).

doc_title: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection › Why it happened
keywords: úroveň je nižší kvůli ochraně marže
summary: A quantity tier is a product discount, so margin protection caps it, never below the price floor. The product page never promises more than checkout; it can promise less while it catches up.
text:
A quantity tier is a product discount like any other, so margin protection
cuts it down to the item's price floor the same way. See
[margin-protection](../concepts/margin-protection.md) for exactly how the floor
is computed.

- **With a cost price:** the tier is capped so the price stays at or above the
  minimum margin.
- **Without a cost price:** the tier is capped at the ceiling percentage for
  products without a cost price.

This can make a higher break look smaller than expected, or, at the extreme,
give nothing extra once the item is already at its floor.

doc_title: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection › How to tell
keywords: úroveň je nižší kvůli ochraně marže
summary: A quantity tier is a product discount, so margin protection caps it, never below the price floor. The product page never promises more than checkout; it can promise less while it catches up.
text:
- [try-a-cart](../tasks/try-a-cart.md) marks the item with the margin floor and
  shows the amount before and after.
- On the product page, the live price already reflects the cap in the rule
  below.

doc_title: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection › The rule: the product page never promises more than checkout
section: The rule: the product page never promises more than checkout
keywords: úroveň je nižší kvůli ochraně marže
summary: A quantity tier is a product discount, so margin protection caps it, never below the price floor. The product page never promises more than checkout; it can promise less while it catches up.
text:
The product page's cap and checkout's cap are computed the same way, but not
always at the exact same instant, so the rule is **never more, sometimes
less**:

- **A market with its own currency:** the product page converts the price
  floor from the shop's currency using Shopify's own exchange rate, rounded
  against the customer, so it never shows a bigger discount than checkout
  will give. It can show a touch less.
- **A variant whose floor is not known yet** — margin protection was just
  turned on or changed, or the cost price was just added, and the floor has
  not finished recomputing: the product page shows no discount promise for
  that variant rather than a guess. It catches up once the recompute
  finishes; checkout always uses the current floor.

doc_title: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection
heading_path: The quantity-tier discount is lower because of margin protection › What you can change
keywords: úroveň je nižší kvůli ochraně marže
summary: A quantity tier is a product discount, so margin protection caps it, never below the price floor. The product page never promises more than checkout; it can promise less while it catches up.
text:
- Lower the minimum margin, or the ceiling for products without a cost price.
- Add the missing cost price in Shopify
  ([products-without-cost-price](products-without-cost-price.md)).
- With Pro, give the product's collection its own margin setting
  ([../concepts/margin-per-collection.md](../concepts/margin-per-collection.md)).

Background: [../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md),
[discount-lowered-by-margin-protection](discount-lowered-by-margin-protection.md).

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text: Check in this order:

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product › 1. The block is not on the product template
section: 1. The block is not on the product template
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text:
**Quantity tiers** in the admin shows whether the block is on your active
theme's product template. If it says it is not, click **Add table to the
product page**. See
[add-tiers-to-the-product-page](../tasks/add-tiers-to-the-product-page.md).

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product › 2. You changed or duplicated the theme
section: 2. You changed or duplicated the theme
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text:
The block is added to one theme. Switching to another theme, publishing a
duplicate, or restoring an older theme version does not carry it over; add it
again on the new theme.

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product › 3. The product has no tier set
section: 3. The product has no tier set
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text:
The table only renders when a tier set applies to the product. A product
listed in a scoped set (by product or by collection) gets only that set,
never the whole-store set, even when the scoped set has no tiers. See
[product-did-not-get-the-global-tiers](product-did-not-get-the-global-tiers.md)
and [../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product › 4. The change is not synced yet
section: 4. The change is not synced yet
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text:
A tier set just saved can take a short moment to reach the storefront config.
Refresh the product page; if it still does not show after a sync completes,
check the Overview for a sync error. See
[../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).

doc_title: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product
heading_path: The quantity-tiers table does not show on the product › 5. Shop is on Free and the set is scoped
section: 5. Shop is on Free and the set is scoped
summary: Why the quantity-tiers block is missing from a product page, in the order to check, from the block not being added to the product having no tiers.
text:
A product-or-collection-scoped tier set is Pro; on Free it is switched off, not
deleted. A product that set was meant for still gets **no** table: a product
listed in a scoped set never falls back to the whole-store set, switched off
or not — Won would rather show nothing than give a discount you did not set up
for that product. See
[../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md](../concepts/plans-free-vs-pro.md) and
[product-did-not-get-the-global-tiers](product-did-not-get-the-global-tiers.md).

doc_title: Show the rewards in the cart
heading_path: Show the rewards in the cart
summary: The app embed shows the rewards in the cart drawer by itself; on the cart page you place them with the Rewards and code block.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Cart rewards**. **The cart on your store** says whether the app embed
   is on. If it is off, click **Turn on in theme** and save in the theme editor.
2. The cart drawer now shows the progress, the gift and the code field by
   itself.
3. For the cart page, click **Add the block to the cart page**. The theme
   editor opens on the cart template with the **Rewards and code** block ready
   to place; put it where you want it and save.

doc_title: Show the rewards in the cart
heading_path: Show the rewards in the cart › Notes
summary: The app embed shows the rewards in the cart drawer by itself; on the cart page you place them with the Rewards and code block.
text:
- Without the block, the panel goes to the top of the cart page's summary. The
  block reserves room for the panel before it fills, so the page moves less
  while it loads.
- The panel takes its fonts and colours from your theme.
- The block shows nothing while no reward is set up.
- What the panel shows: [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

doc_title: Add the sale badge to the product page
heading_path: Add the sale badge to the product page
summary: Add the Sale badge app block to the product page so the badge and Only X left show for a variant on sale.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Clearance → Display and returns**.
2. Choose how the sale shows on the web: *Struck-through price and a "Sale"
   badge* or *Struck-through price, badge and "Only X left"*.
3. Click **Add the badge to the product page**. The theme editor opens on the
   product template with the **Sale badge** block; save the theme there.

doc_title: Add the sale badge to the product page
heading_path: Add the sale badge to the product page › Notes
summary: Add the Sale badge app block to the product page so the badge and Only X left show for a variant on sale.
text:
- The struck-through price is your theme's own (from the compare-at price); it
  needs no block. *Nothing* keeps the sale quiet: no struck price, no badge.
- On a product with several variants the badge names each variant on sale.
- "Only X left" comes from the sale's real quota and disappears at zero.

doc_title: Add the quantity-tiers table to the product page
heading_path: Add the quantity-tiers table to the product page
summary: One click adds the quantity-tiers block to the active theme's product page; the admin shows whether the block is already there.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Quantity discounts**. The screen shows whether the table is already
   on the product page of your active theme.
2. If it is not there, click **Add table to the product page**. This opens the
   theme editor with the block ready to place on the product template; confirm
   there to add it.
3. Once added, Won detects it and the admin shows the table as present.

doc_title: Add the quantity-tiers table to the product page
heading_path: Add the quantity-tiers table to the product page › Notes
summary: One click adds the quantity-tiers block to the active theme's product page; the admin shows whether the block is already there.
text:
- The block reads the tier set that applies to each product (see
  [../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md)) and shows a
  live price that updates as the shopper changes the quantity.
- Choose how the block looks in
  [choose-an-appearance](choose-an-appearance).
- If you change theme, or the block is removed from the template, add it
  again the same way. Troubleshooting:
  [tiers-table-not-showing-on-the-product](../support/tiers-table-not-showing-on-the-product.md).

doc_title: Change the texts on the storefront
heading_path: Change the texts on the storefront
summary: Open Look, expand Storefront texts, type your own wording per language and save; an empty field keeps the default, and the parts in curly braces must stay.
text:
1. Open **Look** and expand **Storefront texts**.
2. Each row is one text in three languages (Czech, Slovak, English). The grey text in a field is the default.
3. Type your own wording where you want it. Keep the parts in curly braces — `{min}`, `{amount}`, `{price}` —
   exactly as they are; the store fills them in.
4. Click **Save**. The store shows the new texts within a moment.

To go back to a default, empty the field and save. A text can have at most 500 characters.

The "pieces left" text of the sale badge is not editable here: it changes its form with the number.

doc_title: Choose an appearance for the quantity-tiers block
heading_path: Choose an appearance for the quantity-tiers block
summary: Pick one of four ready-made looks for the quantity-tiers block; colors and fonts follow the theme automatically.
text:
1. Open **Appearance**.
2. Pick a preset. The preview uses your active theme's own colors and fonts,
   so what you see is what shows on the storefront.
3. Save.

doc_title: Choose an appearance for the quantity-tiers block
heading_path: Choose an appearance for the quantity-tiers block › The presets
summary: Pick one of four ready-made looks for the quantity-tiers block; colors and fonts follow the theme automatically.
text:
| Preset | What it looks like |
|---|---|
| `default` | A clear table of the tiers |
| `highlight` | A table with the tier that applies clearly highlighted |
| `chips` | Compact chips in a row; takes little space |
| `tiles` | Tiles side by side; easy to read on a phone |

Colors and the font always come from the active theme; only the layout
changes between presets. A custom, fully own-designed look is a Pro feature
planned for a later version.

Exact preset list (generated from code):
[../reference/limits.generated.md](../reference/limits.generated.md#block-appearances).
Background: [../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).

heading_path: Schedule a campaign
keywords: try a cart during the campaign
summary: Name the campaign, set its start and end in the store's time, tick the discounts and quantity sets it changes and how, then schedule it and try a cart at its start.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Campaigns** (Pro).
2. Under **New campaign** enter a **name**.
3. Set the **start** and the **end**: a date and a time (HH:MM) each. Times are in
   your store's time zone; the screen says which one and what time it is there now.
4. Under **What the campaign changes**, tick each discount the campaign changes and
   choose:
   - **During the campaign**: *Unchanged*, *Switch on* or *Switch off*;
   - a **new value** (a percent, or an amount per currency) — empty keeps the
     discount's own value. Free shipping can only be switched on or off.
5. Under **Quantity discounts in the campaign**, tick a set to give it other breaks
   during the campaign. The rows start with the set's usual breaks: raise the
   values, or add a break in an empty row. Every quantity must get the same or a
   higher discount than usual; the form says which quantity does not.
6. Click **Schedule campaign**. It is saved and sent to Shopify at once.
7. In the campaign's card click **Try a cart during the campaign** and run a cart:
   the result is what checkout gives at the campaign's start.

The table on the product page shows the campaign's breaks from a minute after the
start until 7 minutes before the end; checkout gives them the whole time.

To stop a running campaign at once, click **End now** in its card. A scheduled one
can be cancelled the same way or deleted.

See [campaigns](../concepts/campaigns.md).

heading_path: Create a discount code
summary: Set up a discount that applies only with a code, add several codes to it, and set usage limits.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Discounts & codes** and start a **New discount**, or the **Welcome code**
   recipe (10 % once per customer).
2. Fill in the name, discount type, value and what it applies to, as for an
   automatic discount ([create-an-automatic-discount](create-an-automatic-discount)).
3. **Applies**: With a code.
4. **Codes**: one per line. Case does not matter. Put several codes into one discount
   when they should give the same thing (for example one code per influencer).
5. Optional, under **More options** → **Limits**: total uses at most, and once per
   customer. Only code discounts have limits.
6. Save.

heading_path: Create a discount code › Before you save
summary: Set up a discount that applies only with a code, add several codes to it, and set usage limits.
text:
- A code can belong to one discount only, in Won and in Shopify. If Shopify already
  has a discount with that code, change the code or move that discount into Won
  ([move-native-discounts](move-native-discounts)).
- The number of **active code discounts** is limited; the editor shows how many you
  have. Adding a code to an existing code discount does not count against it. See
  [../concepts/codes-vs-automatic-discounts.md](../concepts/codes-vs-automatic-discounts.md).

heading_path: Create a discount code › Check it
summary: Set up a discount that applies only with a code, add several codes to it, and set usage limits.
text:
Customers enter the code at checkout. To test without ordering, open
[try-a-cart](try-a-cart), add products and enter the code. It tells you whether the
code applies and, if not, why.

heading_path: Create an automatic discount
summary: Set up a discount that applies by itself (a sale, an amount off the order, free shipping above an amount), from a recipe or blank.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Discounts & codes** and start a **New discount**, or pick a recipe (for
   example "% off everything" or "Free shipping"). A recipe pre-fills the values; you
   only check them.
2. **Name**: customers see it in the cart and at checkout.
3. **Discount type**: Percentage, Fixed amount or Free shipping.
   - A fixed amount has its own value **per currency**. Leave a currency empty and
     the discount is not offered there. Nothing is converted.
4. **Applies to**: Whole order, Products, Collections or Shipping. For products or
   collections, select them.
5. **Applies**: Automatically.
6. Optional, under **More options**:
   - **Minimum order** per currency and/or a minimum quantity, and whether the
     minimum counts the whole cart or only the selected products.
   - **When it runs**: from and until (inclusive), whole days in the shop's time
     zone.
7. Save.

heading_path: Create an automatic discount › Check it
summary: Set up a discount that applies by itself (a sale, an amount off the order, free shipping above an amount), from a recipe or blank.
text:
- The discount's status turns **Live** once it is in Shopify. "Not synced" means it
  is saved but not in Shopify yet; checkout still runs the previous state. See
  [../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md](../concepts/saving-and-syncing.md).
- **Try it in a cart** from the editor shows what a real cart gets. See
  [try-a-cart](try-a-cart).
- If another product discount targets the same items, the better one for the
  customer wins: [../concepts/combining-discounts.md](../concepts/combining-discounts.md).

All options and what each recipe pre-fills:
[../reference/discount-options.generated.md](../reference/discount-options.generated.md).

doc_title: End or reopen a clearance sale
heading_path: End or reopen a clearance sale › End a running sale
summary: End a running sale by hand, or decide what happens with pieces returned after a sale ended.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Clearance**, find the sale under **Running sales**.
2. Click **End the sale**. The prices come back and the sale mark is removed.

doc_title: End or reopen a clearance sale
heading_path: End or reopen a clearance sale › Pieces returned after the end
summary: End a running sale by hand, or decide what happens with pieces returned after a sale ended.
text:
When an order of an ended sale is cancelled or refunded with restock, the
default setting asks you on the **Overview** and on the sale itself:

- **Open again** starts the sale again with the pieces left of its quota. The
  current prices are backed up anew first.
- **Keep it ended** leaves everything as it is.

Choose the behaviour in **Clearance → Display and returns → A return after the sale
ended**. On Free a sale is never opened again.

heading_path: Move Shopify discounts into Won
summary: Move discounts created in Shopify into Won in one click, so the engine counts them and margin protection guards them.
text:
1. Open the **Overview**. **Discounts outside Won** lists the Shopify discounts that
   run next to Won. (Setup offers the same in its second step.)
2. Click **Move** next to one discount, or **Move all**.
3. Read the dialog. It says what happens, **what you lose** (for example the usage
   count) and what to keep in mind for this discount.
4. Confirm. The moved discounts appear under **Moved to Won**, each with Undo.

heading_path: Move Shopify discounts into Won › After the move
summary: Move discounts created in Shopify into Won in one click, so the engine counts them and margin protection guards them.
text:
- If the discount had a fixed amount or a minimum, it now exists in the shop currency
  only. Open it in **Discounts & codes** and add the other currencies, or it is not
  offered there.
- Check a typical cart in [try-a-cart](try-a-cart).
- Discounts that cannot be moved stay in the list with the reason. Won does not count
  them; decide whether to keep them in Shopify.

heading_path: Move Shopify discounts into Won › If a move did not finish
section: If a move did not finish
summary: Move discounts created in Shopify into Won in one click, so the engine counts them and margin protection guards them.
text:
The Overview shows it under unfinished moves. Click **Undo** there; the discount
comes back from the backup.

Background and full list of what is lost:
[../concepts/moving-native-discounts.md](../concepts/moving-native-discounts.md).

heading_path: Prepare for uninstalling
summary: Before uninstalling, click Prepare for uninstalling in Settings, under Plan. It ends running sales (prices back) and restores the Shopify discounts you moved into Won.
text:
After an uninstall the app has no access to your store and **cannot put anything
back**. Do this first — it works on any plan.

1. Open **Settings**, scroll to **Plan** and find **Prepare for uninstalling** (it is
   shown only when there is something to put back). It lists what it will do:
   how many running clearance sales it ends (their prices go back to what they were
   before the sale) and which Shopify discounts it restores (the ones you moved into
   Won with **Move**).
2. Click **Prepare for uninstalling**.
3. Read the result. *Done* with the counts means you can uninstall. If part of it
   failed, the page says what; click again before you uninstall.

What it does **not** do: it does not delete your Won discounts or settings. Shopify
removes the app's discounts together with the app, and the settings are kept for 48
hours in case you reinstall.

If nothing is listed (no running sale, no moved discount), there is nothing to put
back and you can uninstall straight away.

doc_title: Set up a free gift from an amount
heading_path: Set up a free gift from an amount
summary: Pick a product variant as the gift and the order amount per currency; on Pro add more thresholds, a choice of up to 3 gifts and a fallback.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Cart rewards**.
2. In **Free gift**, click **Add a gift**.
3. Enter the **Gift threshold** for each currency of your markets.
4. Click **Pick a gift** and choose the product variant from your store.
5. Optionally pick a **Fallback gift when it is sold out**.
6. Save.

doc_title: Set up a free gift from an amount
heading_path: Set up a free gift from an amount › Pro
summary: Pick a product variant as the gift and the order amount per currency; on Pro add more thresholds, a choice of up to 3 gifts and a fallback.
text:
- **Add another threshold** builds a ladder (for example a gift from
  1 500 Kč and another from 3 000 Kč). Every threshold the order reaches gets
  its own gift.
- **Gift (a choice of up to 3)**: pick up to 3 variants; the customer chooses
  one in the cart.

doc_title: Set up a free gift from an amount
heading_path: Set up a free gift from an amount › Notes
summary: Pick a product variant as the gift and the order amount per currency; on Pro add more thresholds, a choice of up to 3 gifts and a fallback.
text:
- The gift is a real product: it needs stock like any other item. A sold-out
  gift is not offered (the fallback is, when set).
- At checkout 1 item of the gift is always free. See
  [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).
- **Count other discounts toward the gift threshold** decides what happens when
  a code takes the order below the threshold; see
  [../support/discount-code-and-the-gift.md](../support/discount-code-and-the-gift.md).
- Check the result in **Try a cart**: a cart over the threshold shows the gift
  line, free. See [try-a-cart](try-a-cart).
- The cart adds the gift only with the app embed on. See
  [add-the-cart-panel-to-the-cart-page](add-the-cart-panel-to-the-cart-page).

doc_title: Set up free shipping from an amount
heading_path: Set up free shipping from an amount
summary: Turn on free shipping in Cart rewards and enter the order amount for each currency of your markets.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Cart rewards**.
2. In **Free shipping**, switch on **Offer free shipping from an amount**.
3. Enter the amount for each currency of your markets (for example
   `1 000` in CZK and `40` in EUR). Amounts are in the currency's normal units.
4. Save.

doc_title: Set up free shipping from an amount
heading_path: Set up free shipping from an amount › Notes
summary: Turn on free shipping in Cart rewards and enter the order amount for each currency of your markets.
text:
- The amount counts the items in the cart before discounts; the free gift does
  not count. See [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).
- A currency left empty gets no free shipping; the screen names the market. See
  [../support/free-shipping-missing-in-a-market.md](../support/free-shipping-missing-in-a-market.md).
- Whether free shipping adds up with your other discounts follows the
  combination switches in Settings: see
  [switch-combination-categories](switch-combination-categories).
- The cart on your store shows "X more for free shipping" only with the app
  embed on.

heading_path: Set up quantity discounts
summary: Add quantity breaks to the tier set, choose a percentage or a fixed amount per currency, and pick how quantity is counted.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Quantity discounts**.
2. Add a **tier**: from how many items, and the discount — a percentage, or a
   fixed amount off per item in each market's currency. Add more tiers for
   more thresholds. A set is one kind only (every tier a percent, or every
   tier an amount), and each tier must be worth at least as much as the one
   before it; the form will not let you save otherwise.
3. Choose how items are **counted**: each variant separately, or all variants
   of the product together. (With Pro, also across the whole cart.)
4. Save.

heading_path: Set up quantity discounts › Scoping (Pro)
summary: Add quantity breaks to the tier set, choose a percentage or a fixed amount per currency, and pick how quantity is counted.
text:
By default one **global** set applies to every product. With Pro you can add
more sets, each scoped to chosen products or collections; the first matching
set wins over the global one. See
[../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).

heading_path: Set up quantity discounts › After saving
summary: Add quantity breaks to the tier set, choose a percentage or a fixed amount per currency, and pick how quantity is counted.
text:
- Add the table to the product page: see
  [add-tiers-to-the-product-page](add-tiers-to-the-product-page).
- A tier competes with other product discounts on the same item; the better
  one for the customer wins. Margin protection can still lower it.
- Check the result in [try-a-cart](try-a-cart) before relying on it.

heading_path: Set up quantity discounts › Running out of room
summary: Add quantity breaks to the tier set, choose a percentage or a fixed amount per currency, and pick how quantity is counted.
text:
Every tier set you save shares one small storage budget across the whole
shop. With many sets, many tiers per set, or amounts in many currencies, you
can run out of room before hitting the per-set tier limit; if a save would
not fit, the admin says so and nothing is saved.

Background: [../concepts/quantity-tiers.md](../concepts/quantity-tiers.md).
Exact limits: [../reference/limits.generated.md](../reference/limits.generated.md).

heading_path: Start a clearance sale
summary: Pick a variant, enter the pieces to sell and the percent, optionally an end date and price lists, and start the sale.
text:
1. Open **Discounts → Clearance**.
2. In **New sale**, click **Pick a variant** and choose the product and its variant.
3. Enter **Pieces to sell** (the quota) and **Discount (%)**.
4. Optionally pick an **End** date. The sale ends at the start of that day in your
   store's time zone.
5. Tick the market **price lists** whose fixed price should get the discount too.
6. Click **Start the sale**.

heading_path: Start a clearance sale › Notes
summary: Pick a variant, enter the pieces to sell and the percent, optionally an end date and price lists, and start the sale.
text:
- One sale per variant at a time; up to the store limit in
  [../reference/limits.generated.md](../reference/limits.generated.md).
- A ticked price list without a fixed price for this variant is left as it is;
  the result says how many.
- How it works: [../concepts/clearance.md](../concepts/clearance.md).

heading_path: Start the Pro trial
summary: Open Settings, scroll to Plan, click Try Pro free for 14 days, approve the subscription on Shopify's page, and you are back in the app on Pro.
text:
1. Open **Settings** and scroll to **Plan**.
2. Click **Try Pro free for 14 days**.
3. Shopify's confirmation page opens. Check the price (29 USD a month after the
   trial) and click **Approve**.
4. You land back in the app on **Plan**: it says *You are trying Pro until …* with the trial's
   last day. Your discounts are sent to Shopify again so Pro settings apply at
   checkout right away.

If you close Shopify's page without approving, nothing changes and nothing is
charged. To stop: **Cancel Pro** on the same page, see
[billing-and-downgrade](../concepts/billing-and-downgrade.md).

heading_path: Switch combination categories in Settings
summary: Settings lets you switch, by category, whether Won's discounts add up or compete, instead of the fixed defaults.
text:
By default Won combines discounts one fixed way: product discounts on the
same item compete (the better one wins) and never add up — that one is not a
switch — while product discounts add up with order and shipping discounts.
See [combining-discounts](../concepts/combining-discounts.md).

1. Open **Settings → Combining discounts**.
2. For each switchable category — **Clearance with other discounts**,
   **Product discounts with order discounts**, **Product discounts with
   shipping discounts**, **Order discounts with shipping discounts** —
   switch it between adding up and competing. Each switch explains in plain
   words what flipping it does.
3. Save. One save applies every change at once.

heading_path: Switch combination categories in Settings › Check the effect
summary: Settings lets you switch, by category, whether Won's discounts add up or compete, instead of the fixed defaults.
text:
Changing these switches can change what a shopper pays on carts that already
have several discounts. Before relying on a new setting, check it in
[try-a-cart](try-a-cart) with a cart that has more than one discount.

This setting is store-wide and available on Free. Choosing combinations **per
discount** (so discount A stacks with C but not B) is Pro; see
[pro-combinations](../concepts/pro-combinations.md).

Exact default table: [../reference/combination-defaults.generated.md](../reference/combination-defaults.generated.md).

heading_path: Try a cart
summary: (Pro) Build a test cart with products, a market, discounts with a code and a day, and see which Won discounts apply at checkout and why. Nothing is ordered.
text:
Try a cart runs the same engine as checkout on real Shopify prices. Nothing is
ordered. It is part of the Pro plan; on Free the page shows what it does.

1. Open **Settings → Tools → Try a cart** (or **Try it in a cart** from a discount).
2. **Add products** and set quantities.
3. Pick the **Market & currency**. Prices come from Shopify for that market; a
   product without a price in that currency cannot be calculated.
4. Optional: tick the **discounts with a code** the customer would enter. The list
   holds your Won discounts; the app fills in the code. Automatic discounts are
   listed as applying on their own. A discount that cannot apply for the chosen
   market or day is greyed out with the reason.
5. Optional: **When**. "Now", or "Custom date and time" in the shop's time zone, to
   check a scheduled discount or a campaign at an exact minute; a campaign's
   **Try a cart during the campaign** fills both in.
6. **Calculate**.

heading_path: Try a cart › Reading the result
summary: (Pro) Build a test cart with products, a market, discounts with a code and a day, and see which Won discounts apply at checkout and why. Nothing is ordered.
text:
- **What applies**: the discount per item, the order discount and the total the
  customer pays.
- Each discount and code has a sentence saying why it applies or not ("needs 1 more
  item", "another discount is better", "not valid in EUR").
- Items at the margin floor are marked, with the discount before and after.
- Cart rewards: free shipping and how much is left to it and to the gift. A
  reached gift threshold adds the gift line, tagged **Gift**, exactly as the cart
  on your store would; it is free. With a choice of gifts (Pro) the first one
  offered is shown. See [../concepts/cart-rewards.md](../concepts/cart-rewards.md).

heading_path: Try a cart › "Checkout may differ"
summary: (Pro) Build a test cart with products, a market, discounts with a code and a day, and see which Won discounts apply at checkout and why. Nothing is ordered.

heading_path: Turn on margin protection
summary: Switch margin protection on, set the minimum margin and the ceiling for products without a cost price, and check where it lowers discounts.
text:
1. Open **Margin protection** and **Turn on margin protection**.
2. **Minimum margin**: the margin a discounted item must keep, measured like
   Shopify's product margin. Leave it empty to only never go below the cost price.
3. **Products without a cost price: discount at most**: the ceiling for products with
   no cost price in Shopify.
4. Save.

heading_path: Turn on margin protection › After saving
summary: Switch margin protection on, set the minimum margin and the ceiling for products without a cost price, and check where it lowers discounts.
text:
- Won reads the cost prices from Shopify in the background and shows the progress.
  Until a product's cost price is read, the ceiling protects it.
- The **Cost prices** part shows how many products have no cost price. Add them in
  Shopify on the product, in the variant's pricing; Won picks them up by itself.

heading_path: Turn on margin protection › Check the effect
summary: Switch margin protection on, set the minimum margin and the ceiling for products without a cost price, and check where it lowers discounts.
text:
- The discount editor notes when protection lowers that discount.
- [try-a-cart](try-a-cart) marks items at the margin floor, with the discount before
  and after.
- With Pro, **Where protection steps in** lists every discount and variant it
  lowers, and **Settings per collection** sets other values for chosen collections
  ([../concepts/margin-per-collection.md](../concepts/margin-per-collection.md)).

Protection never blocks an order and guards only Won discounts. Background:
[../concepts/margin-protection.md](../concepts/margin-protection.md). Values and
defaults: [../reference/margin-settings.generated.md](../reference/margin-settings.generated.md).

heading_path: Undo a move
summary: Put a moved discount back into Shopify from Won's backup, and why to do it before uninstalling the app.
text:
1. Open the **Overview** and find the discount under **Moved to Won**.
2. Click **Undo** and read **What changes**.
3. Confirm. Won removes its discount, checks that Shopify no longer runs it, and
   creates the discount in Shopify again from the backup.

heading_path: Undo a move › What changes
summary: Put a moved discount back into Shopify from Won's backup, and why to do it before uninstalling the app.
text:
The discount comes back as a **new** Shopify discount: a new ID, the usage count from
zero, and the usage limit set to the uses that were left. Changes you made to the Won
discount after the move are lost; the backup is the discount as it was before the
move.

heading_path: Undo a move › Before uninstalling Won
summary: Put a moved discount back into Shopify from Won's backup, and why to do it before uninstalling the app.
text:
Moved discounts run through Won and stop working when the app is uninstalled. Undo
every move first.

Background: [../concepts/moving-native-discounts.md](../concepts/moving-native-discounts.md).
